items.title: moving a FIELD out of an OWNED aggregate is refused for a resource field ("v1 has no partial moves") — A142's pipe nodes do exactly that (`self.up.start(..)` under `own self`); RULED: allow the move when the aggregate is owned, otherwise DEAD afterwards, and has NO `Drop` anywhere inside it (read as a destructure)
items.discussion: native-44 (Order 44); repro `sweeps/order44/native-44/finds/p_field_move.vl`; B463 (the per-instantiation re-check would otherwise refuse every generic node); spec §6.8's affine rules; A142 R29
items.body: Today a generic node compiles only because the partial-move rule is not re-checked per instantiation (B463's class of hole). The owner ruled door (a) (2026-09-29): a field may be moved out of an aggregate the function OWNS (`own self`, an owned local) when no later use of the aggregate or its other fields exists and no `Drop` is anywhere in the aggregate's type (the F56 test) — Rust's partial move for non-`Drop` types; a later use of the moved field or the whole aggregate is the ordinary use-after-move error naming the field. Rejected: (b) a destructuring `let` (a new form, every node rewritten), (c) `Option` fields + `take`. Pins: a node's `self.up.start(..)` under a resource instantiation accepted; a use of `self` after the move refused; an aggregate with a `Drop` member still refused; B463's pins unchanged. Sizing S–M; solver-44, immediately after B463.

items.title: a resource can never become `dyn` ("a trait object's teardown would have to be dispatched through its table") — A142's selectors with arms of different types and `TransientSource::latest()`/`is_pending()` return `dyn Flow`/`dyn Pipe`; RULED: a resource with NO `Drop` anywhere inside it may become a trait object (there is no teardown to dispatch); a resource with `Drop` stays refused
items.discussion: native-44 (Order 44); repros `sweeps/order44/native-44/finds/r5_dyn.vl`, `p_dyn.vl`; F56 (the same Drop-less test on the native side); A142 §3.2/§5; B4 / trait-objects.md §8 (drop)
items.body: The trait object of a Drop-less resource is itself a resource (move-only) — coercing into `dyn` moves the value, and the `dyn` value obeys the affine rules (no copy, a use after move refused). Both backends: JS carries the pair as today; native (F56's emission) must build the erased pair for a resource without cloning (native-44 pins it after the analyzer change). Pins: a Drop-less resource into `dyn Trait` accepted and moved; a second use refused; a `Drop` resource into `dyn` still refused with today's message; A142's mixed-arm selector shape. Sizing S–M; solver-44 after B469, native parity in native-44.
